blocks.text: This article provides a summary of all new features and enhancements for Zscaler Deception.
The illusionblack.com cloud represents all clouds, and updates to specific clouds might take a few weeks to deploy. Some functions are not available until deployment completes.
The following new datasets for different application vulnerabilities were added:

table: Remote Code Execution vulnerability caused by .NET deserialization flaw in the Ad Hoc Transfer module. The adversaries leverage a vulnerability associated with the improper handling of file uploads within the HTTP module.

Improper Authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers with network access to the Confluence instance to restore the database of the Confluence instance and eventually execute arbitrary system commands.

blocks.text: To learn more, see About Vulnerable Application Datasets (CVE Datasets).
The following new ThreatParse Rules that detect exploits of different application vulnerabilities were added:

table: Remote Code Execution vulnerability that allows unauthenticated adversaries to execute code through the exploitation of the ASP.NET TemplateParser, which is crucial in ASP.NET Web Forms for parsing various source files.

Remote Code Execution vulnerability caused by .NET deserialization flaw in the Ad Hoc Transfer module. The adversaries leverage a vulnerability associated with the improper handling of file uploads within the HTTP module.
A web service authentication bypass vulnerability that potentially allows unauthenticated adversaries with network access to execute remote commands.

Remote Code Execution vulnerability due to a YAML deserialization flaw. This can allow an attacker to send a specially crafted obsolete API call and thereby execute arbitrary code, obtain sensitive data, and execute other unauthorized operations.

Access Control Bypass vulnerability in Adobe ColdFusion, which allows a remote attacker to bypass the ColdFusion mechanisms that restrict unauthenticated external access to the ColdFusion Administrator.
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Adobe ColdFusion that could result in arbitrary code execution without any user interaction.
Remote Code Execution vulnerability in PaperCut NG that allows a remote unauthenticated user to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM.

Broken Access Control vulnerability in the Atlassian Confluence Data Center and Server that allows an attacker to create unauthorized Confluence administrator accounts and access Confluence instances.

Improper Authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers with network access to the Confluence instance to restore the database of the Confluence instance and eventually execute arbitrary system commands.

blocks.text: To learn more, see About ThreatParse Rules.

The event score for events that match multiple ThreatParse rules is now calculated by computing the highest score among the matching rules, instead of adding scores of all matching ThreatParse rules. For each event, the score is displayed in the Event Details pane, which can be accessed by clicking an event from the Event Logs page (Investigate > View Extended Details > Event Logs).
See image.
To learn more, see About Event Logs.

Zscaler Deception runs a scheduler every hour to update the list of CrowdStrike-contained endpoints in the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. This ensures the removal of contained devices from the Zscaler Posture Control Admin Portal if the containment is lifted for those devices manually from the CrowdStrike Falcon Insight Platform.
To learn more, see Viewing the Contained Attacker Details.
Options to delete settings for Cloud Deception with Microsoft Azure (Deceive > Cloud Deception > Azure > Settings) and Amazon Web Services (Deceive > Cloud Deception > AWS> Settings) are supported.
See image.
To learn more, see Deleting Azure Deception Settings and Deleting AWS Deception Settings.

blocks.item: For the purpose of licensing, the total number of landmine decoys consumed from the allocated landmine license quota is computed as a sum of:
Zscaler Client Connector Landmines: This counts the number of unique Zscaler Client Connector users across all landmines in the active state.
Standalone Landmines: This counts the number of unique hostnames across all landmines in the active state.
Agentless Landmines: This counts the number of unique hostnames across all landmines in the active state.

blocks.text: Landmine agents (ZCC Integrated and Standalone) whose last check-in time is older than 7 days are considered inactive and are removed from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. The landmine agentless is always active.

blocks.item: The following user interface changes were made to the Landmine Agents page (Deceive > Landmine > Agents):
The System User Name column that shows the list of users that are logged in to the system was added.
The Client Connector Users column that shows the list of users that are logged in to Zscaler Client Connector was renamed to Client Connector User.
The Agentless column was replaced with the Type column, which allows you to filter the table based on the type of landmine agent (ZCC Integrated, Standalone, and Agentless).
The option to filter the values in the drop-down menu based on user input was added to the Version column.
The option to filter the agent table using a date range was added to the First Seen and the Last Seen columns.

blocks.text: You can add tags to decoys and other resources deployed on the Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud directly from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. Tags allow you to identify and distinguish the resources deployed by Zscaler Deception. The option to add tags is available on the Cloud Deception - AWS page (Deceive > Cloud Deception > AWS > Settings).
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring and Managing Tags for AWS Resources.

blocks.heading: Apple Silicon Support for Landmine Agent and Agentless

blocks.text: Landmine Agent and Agentless are supported on Mac computers with Apple Silicon. You can download the installers from the Download Agent drop-down menu under Deceive > Landmine > Agents.
See image.

blocks.heading: Apply Landmine Policies to Zscaler Client Connector Users

blocks.text: You can configure landmine policies with Zscaler Client Connecter users as its criteria.

To learn more, see Creating a Landmine Policy.

blocks.heading: Cloud Deception with Microsoft Azure and AWS

blocks.text: You can integrate Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services (AWS) with Zscaler Deception and deploy decoy resources specific to those public cloud platforms. You can deploy decoys to detect malicious activities originating from adversaries within or outside your organization, depending on the type and configuration of the decoys.

You can integrate Microsoft Azure with Zscaler Deception and deploy various Azure-specific resources as decoys. The following Azure-specific resources can be configured as decoys from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal:
See image.
To learn more, see About Cloud Deception with Azure and Setting Up Cloud Deception with Microsoft Azure.

You can integrate AWS with Zscaler Deception and deploy various AWS-specific resources as decoys. The following AWS-specific resources can be configured as decoys from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal:
See image.
To learn more, see About Cloud Deception with AWS and Setting Up Cloud Deception with AWS.
You can deploy lures for Azure and AWS decoys on endpoints using the following landmine policies.
Depending on the type of decoy, you can also configure other lures and detect adversarial behaviors.
To learn more, see Configuring Lures Using Azure Decoys and Configuring Lures Using AWS Decoys.

The existing AWS Decoys feature (Deceive > AWS Decoys) is deprecated and all existing AWS IAM decoys and AWS S3 decoys will no longer work. Customers using these existing AWS decoys should migrate to new Cloud Deception with AWS manually.

To learn more, see Taking Action From the Dashboard and Configuring a Retention Policy.

blocks.heading: Expiration Period for Connection Code in Decoy Connectors

blocks.text: The expiration period for the connection code in Decoy Connectors has been changed to 12 hours.
To learn more, see Adding and Connecting a Decoy Connector to the Zscaler Deception.

Zscaler Deception supports integration with Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) to contain and isolate Zscaler Client Connector users who interact with landmine decoys by blocking internet access to those users across devices.
See image.
To learn more, see Zscaler Deception and Zscaler Internet Access Deployment Guide.

See image.
To learn more, see Deception and Sumo Logic Deployment Guide.

blocks.heading: Validation for Landmine Agent Service Name

blocks.text: Zscaler Deception validates the user-provided landmine agent service name and prevents users from configuring a name that matches the name of a default service to avoid landmine agent failures.
To learn more, see Customizing Landmine Installer.

blocks.heading: Zscaler Client Connector-Integrated Landmine Deception License Changes

blocks.text: The license calculation has changed for users deploying endpoint deception with Zscaler Client Connector. For Zscaler Client Connector - integrated landmines, the license is calculated per user logged into Zscaler Client Connector. For standalone landmines, licenses are still calculated per system.
To learn more, see Ranges and Limitations.

blocks.heading: Create a Zero Trust Network Decoy of a Real or Production Application in ZPA

blocks.text: You can add Zero Trust Network decoys to existing real application segments in Zscaler Private Access (ZPA). The application segments must be on unused ports and have at least one FQDN configured.
Zscaler Deception doesn't allow you to configure an IP address for Zero Trust Network or ZPA decoys. Alerts are generated only for connections to the decoy FQDN.
See image.
To learn more, see Creating a Zero Trust Network Decoy and About ZPA Applications.

blocks.heading: Create and Deploy a Deception Strategy

blocks.text: The Deception Strategy feature enables you to leverage the ready-to-use personalities or tags to quickly configure Internal decoys, Threat Intelligence (TI) decoys, Active Directory (AD) decoys, and Landmine policies on a single page. You can configure realistic-looking decoys that have services, names, or configurations that mimic real assets on your network.
By default, Zscaler Deception provides built-in strategies that cover various business use cases to detect threats. You can create custom strategies for your business needs.
See image.
To learn more, see About Deception Strategy and Creating a Strategy.
After you create strategies, you can deploy them using Internal or Zero Trust Network (ZTN) decoys.
See image.
To learn more, see About Deploy Strategy and Deploying a Strategy.
You can configure a response rule to specify actions that the CrowdStrike solution can take when Zscaler Deception detects IOC IP, IOC Hash, and IOA process tree activities on an endpoint.

When IOC and IOA activities are detected, the response rule is triggered and IOCs and IOAs of the attacker's process are forwarded to the CrowdStrike solution with the required action specified in the response rule.
See image.
To learn more, see Zscaler Deception and CrowdStrike Deployment Guide and Viewing the Contained Attacker Details.

blocks.heading: Custom Response Headers for Threat Intelligence Decoys and Web Services On Internal Decoys

blocks.text: Threat Intelligence (TI) decoys and web services on Internal network decoys have custom response headers that you can use to manipulate the HTTP response headers. The response headers are visible in a browser when an adversary accesses a TI or Internal network decoy. Custom headers make the decoy look realistic, so that an adversary continues to interact with the decoy for a longer time.
See image.
To learn more, see Creating a Threat Intelligence Decoy.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring a Web Service on a Network Decoy.

blocks.text: You can configure the default expiration period (in hours) when configuring the containment integration with the Palo Alto Networks or Fortinet solution. The same expiration period is also applicable to the response rules.
See image.
To learn more, see Zscaler Deception and Palo Alto Networks Deployment Guide.
See image.
To learn more, see Zscaler Deception and Fortinet Deployment Guide.
On the Investigate page, you can export a list of evidence files that are collected as a CSV or JSON file.
See image.
To learn more, see About Evidence File and Exporting Evidence Details.
Zscaler Deception provides internal (built-in) safe processes. You can show or hide these internal safe processes on the Safe Processes page (Deceive > Landmine > Safe Processes).

To learn more, see About Safe Processes and Configuring a Safe Process.

blocks.heading: Managing ZPA and Threat Intelligence Components

blocks.text: If the following Zscaler Deception components are managed by Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) or Threat Intelligence (TI), you must contact Zscaler Support to manage them (i.e., edit, delete, etc.):

blocks.item: Decoy Connector (ZPA and TI): Edit, obtain a connection code, configure proxy, and delete.
Aggregator: Edit, obtain a connection code, and delete.
Service back end: Edit, obtain a connection code, and delete.
Subnet or interface: Edit or delete.

blocks.heading: Quarantine Device With VMware Carbon Black Endpoint Standard

blocks.text: Zscaler Deception integration with VMWare Carbon Black Endpoint Standard supports the ability to block network communication with other devices by quarantining the infected endpoint, instead of using isolate policies to achieve the same outcome.
See image.
To learn more, see Zscaler Deception and VMware Carbon Black Endpoint Standard Deployment Guide.

Landmine processes that detect defense evasion sometimes generate false positives when tripped by security processes, such as an antivirus or Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) scan. Zscaler Deception allows you to configure safe landmine processes that don’t generate events when accessed by legitimate security processes. Alerts are generated only when an attacker interacts with these landmine processes.
